work.title: PM/RCM migration with explicit provider crosswalk and independent control retention
authority: Direct user decision: freeze RR-MIGRATION-001 as PROVEN and canonize population-specific source supersession.

intent.productGoal: Transform unseen physician-group source files into a lineaged canonical QoR model and formula-driven draft work product without manual rebuilding or forced financial balance.
intent.capability: Treat a complete native PM/RCM cohort as authoritative for duplicated transaction populations, resolve providers only through its explicit crosswalk, retain independent root controls, reconcile those controls independently, and maintain draft-versus-release gate authority.
architecturalIntent: Source supersession is evaluated per financial population, not by ZIP folder or package membership.
Native provider identity is system-qualified and authoritative only through the supplied explicit crosswalk.
Independent A/R, GL, bank, and reference controls survive native transaction supersession and remain run-bound evidence.
invariants: Unreconciled differences are surfaced and never balanced by an inferred or hidden entry.
No provider identity is resolved by display name, unqualified identifier, or inferred normalization when an explicit crosswalk is absent.
G3/G4 calculation success does not confer G7 release authority.
acceptanceEvidence: Run 3f1715a9-4c60-4097-bb11-d141f29b3d04 from the unchanged staged Challenge F ZIP.
Run-bound reconciliation, migration-coverage, and gate observations recorded in docs/RR_MIGRATION_001_REPORT.md.
Source-router regression test and ADR-006 router contract.

decisions.decision: Freeze the semantic proof as RR-MIGRATION-001 rather than treat Challenge F as its durable identity.
decisions.rationale: Corpus letters are transport labels; the semantic capability and immutable run/source binding are the auditable proof identity.

decisions.decision: Make source supersession population-specific in the ingestion/router contract.
decisions.rationale: Native transactions replace duplicate claims/payments, while independent A/R, GL, bank, and reference controls remain necessary for a non-forced reconciliation proof.

observedBehaviour: The rerun accepted all four native populations with separate LEGACY_PM and NEW_RCM attribution, no rejected rows, and complete 24-entry crosswalk coverage.
All cash-to-GL, ERA-to-bank, matched-cash-to-GL, and A/R-to-GL controls matched with zero difference.
G3 and G4 passed while G7 remained blocked by G0, G2, G5, and G6; the workbench compiled a draft workbook over HTTP 200.

evidence.result: Four independent reconciliation controls matched at $0.00 difference; zero open findings; G3 and G4 passed.
Records source hashes, native contributions, crosswalk coverage, reconciliation controls, and gated-export outcome.
Regression proof requires native migration sources to supersede only duplicate root claims/payments while retaining A/R, GL, bank, and reference controls.
Accepted router contract establishes the population-specific supersession rule and explicit-crosswalk authority boundary.

learning.recurringPattern: Folder-wide routing decisions conflate duplicate transaction populations with independent financial controls.
durableKnowledge: Native PM/RCM source files may replace duplicate transactions without displacing root A/R, GL, bank, or reference controls.
Crosswalk authority is system-qualified; NEW_RCM identifiers retain the supplied N- prefix and are not display-name candidates.
A complete deterministic migration proof may support G3/G4 while governance gates still limit output to a draft workbook.
